input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the walk over exc.__cause__ has no cycle guard, so a chain that loops back on itself never reaches None
- failure path: an exception raised with `raise e from e`, or two exceptions that cause each other, makes retry_if_exception_cause_type spin forever at full CPU; the stop conditions never run and the caller hangs

Reviewer finding
- description: Removing the `seen` set makes the `__cause__` walk loop forever if the exception chain contains a cycle and no cause matches `exception_cause_types`.
- rationale: Trigger: an exception whose __cause__ chain loops back on itself, e.g. a.__cause__ = b and b.__cause__ = a, is raised and retried with a retry predicate on exception causes. Mechanism: the while loop now only stops on None or a match, so it never terminates on the cycle. Impact: the retry decision hangs the calling thread instead of returning False.
critique: The finding says the __cause__ walk has no cycle guard, since the seen set was removed. A cyclic chain therefore loops forever and hangs the retry decision. This is the same faulty operation and failure mechanism as the label.
